sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation of Aerospace Engineering in Ireland
sections.lead: \\Accreditation\\ is a crucial factor when choosing an engineering degree as it affects professional development and future registration opportunities.

items: Engineers Ireland accredits eligible engineering programs to recognized educational and professional standards.
Check before you enroll:
If the specific program is \\accredited\.
What level of qualification the accreditation is for.
If the accreditation is current for the year you are expected to graduate.
If you require additional education or work experience for your career goals.

An \\accredited engineering degree\\ does not automatically guarantee a job, professional registration or recognition in every country. If you are planning to work in India or elsewhere after graduation, check the relevant professional and qualification recognition requirements.

faqs.q: Is Aerospace Engineering available in Ireland after 12th?
faqs.a: Yes. \\SETU\\ has a four year BEng (Honours) in Aerospace Engineering. \\University of Limerick\\ has Aeronautical Engineering. International applicants must meet country-specific academic and English language requirements for each university.

faqs.q: \\Q2. How long is the Aerospace Engineering degree in Ireland?
faqs.a: The dedicated undergraduate programs described in this guide generally take \\four years\\ for a bachelor's qualification. Some routes allow an additional year for an integrated master's degree.

faqs.q: \\Q3. What is the tuition fee for international students?\\
faqs.a: SETU has published general guidance on international undergraduate fees suggesting \\€13,500–€14,500 per year. Aerospace Engineering fee structure for your intake. Fees at the University of Limerick to be checked separately. Living costs are additional.

faqs.q: \\Q4. What are the essential subjects for Aerospace Engineering admissions?\\
faqs.a: Mathematics is of special importance and Physics is of great relevance. Please see the official entry requirements of the university for the subjects and grades required from your school qualification.

faqs.q: \\Q5. What are the jobs that I can get in Ireland after doing Aerospace Engineering?
faqs.a: Graduates can seek employment in \\aircraft design, aerodynamics, aircraft structures, avionics, propulsion, flight testing, UAV technology and aerospace manufacturing. Career outcomes are a function of technical skills, experience, vacancies and employability.
